s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with tremors, weakness, and speech difficulties
salient_findings: Episodes of spasms and tremors in the right hand and forearm
key_facts: Woman in her mid-60s
Initial carpal tunnel release surgery
Recurring tremors
Referred to a neurologist 7 months later
Developed progressive right-sided weakness over 3 months
Experienced dysarthria, hand tremors, and slurred speech
Gait instability
Brain MRI showed hyperintensities in bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter and other areas
No contrast enhancement on T1-weighted MRI
Brain biopsy showed CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ cells
Cerebrospinal fluid contained lymphoma cells
Bone marrow was negative for lymphoma cells

shortlist.label: Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Brain biopsy showed CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ cells and cerebrospinal fluid contained lymphoma cells

shortlist.label: Intravascular Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neurological decline with tremors, weakness, and speech difficulties, and presence of lymphoma cells in cerebrospinal fluid

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid Granulomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation and presence of lymphoma cells in cerebrospinal fluid

shortlist.label: Neurolymphomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neurological decline and presence of lymphoma cells in cerebrospinal fluid

shortlist.label: Gliomatosis Cerebri
shortlist.why_kept: Extensive non-enhancing lesions in bilateral cerebral hemispheres on MRI

raw.rationale: The presence of lymphoma cells in the cerebrospinal fluid, brain biopsy showing CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ cells, and brain MRI showing hyperintensities in bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter without contrast enhancement are consistent with Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma (PCNSL). The absence of lymphoma cells in the bone marrow also supports a primary CNS origin.

rejected.label: Intravascular Lymphoma
rejected.why: Intravascular lymphoma typically presents with skin lesions, fever, and neurological symptoms, but the imaging and biopsy findings in this case do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid Granulomatosis
rejected.why: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis is a rare condition characterized by lung involvement and angiocentric lesions, which are not mentioned in this case.

rejected.label: Neurolymphomatosis
rejected.why: Neurolymphomatosis refers to the infiltration of the nervous system by lymphoma, but the term is not specific enough to explain the imaging and biopsy findings in this case.

rejected.label: Gliomatosis Cerebri
rejected.why: Gliomatosis cerebri is a rare condition characterized by diffuse infiltration of the brain by glial cells, but the presence of lymphoma cells in the cerebrospinal fluid and brain biopsy findings are not consistent with this diagnosis.
